title: Tighter sign-in checks
summary: Sign-in now asks org admins for a second factor before any session is granted, session cookies slide their expiry on activity, and the legacy token endpoint is gone.

scenarios.action: sign in with a valid password when two-factor authentication is enforced for admins
scenarios.outcome: the user is asked for a second-factor code before any session cookie is set

scenarios.action: submit the login form with a registered email and the correct password
scenarios.outcome: the user lands on the tasks page, the session cookie is set, and its expiry slides forward on each authenticated request

scenarios.action: open a protected page with an expired session cookie
scenarios.outcome: the session is rejected server-side and the user is redirected to the login page

scenarios.action: open a protected page with a cookie signed by a foreign key
scenarios.outcome: the foreign-key cookie rejection was removed together with the legacy token endpoint
